prose.summary: Reconciled source purposes: [1] Define install, load, enable, disable and reload as separate UserModule lifecycle operations, preserving inert-definition and explicit-capability boundaries. [2] Define explicit UserModule lifecycle states from discovered/installed definition through registered, configured, enabled, loaded/running and stopped/error states.

semantics.dependency_rule: Missing dependencies hard-fail; they are never auto-enabled.
semantics.disable_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] Disable removes active capability without deleting the authoritative definition unless uninstall semantics explicitly do so. [2] Disable removes runtime availability without changing canonical module identity.
semantics.enable_rule: Enable changes capability presence subject to explicit boot/profile/dependency rules.
semantics.failure_rule: Load/start failure is visible and does not silently change module identity or enable dependencies.
semantics.inert_rule: Discovery/install/registration does not execute the module.
semantics.install_rule: Install writes definition/source material but does not execute or automatically enable the module.
semantics.load_rule: Reconciled source clauses: [1] Load parses/registers inert definitions. [2] Load validates module identity/type/schema/dependencies before activation.
semantics.migration_rule: Breaking module semantic changes follow canonical identity/versioning rules.
semantics.reload_rule: Reload reconciles source-owned definition state and preserves unrelated runtime-owned state.
semantics.separation_rule: Installed, registered, enabled and running are distinct states.
semantics.start_rule: Only lifecycle-capable module types/instances enter running state where applicable.
semantics.stop_rule: Stop releases owned runtime resources without deleting definition/installation.
